app.name: Sastras AI
app.what_it_does: Reads a writer's own blog, learns how they write, then writes new blog posts in their voice and delivers them to their WordPress site. It can run by hand or on a schedule.

flows.name: Sign up and connect a site
flows.trigger: A new writer opens the app

steps.what: Sign up or log in
Enter the site address or sitemap address
The app sends the event site/analyze.requested and answers at once. The work runs in the background.
Connect a way to publish (optional at this point): WordPress plugin or WordPress login

flows.name: Analyze the site and learn the writer's style
flows.trigger: Event site/analyze.requested (new site, or the Re-analyze button)

steps.what: Mark the site as being analyzed
Read the sitemap, scrape each post (title, text, headings, meta, date, links), save the posts. Obeys robots.txt.
Split posts into chunks and embed them (Voyage) into pgvector. This is the memory the writing agents search.
Build the style profile: tone, average length, heading structure, sentence style, point of view, common phrases
Group the posts into topics, using the post embeddings
Mark the site ready. Create its Autopilot settings, switched off.
Send ideas/suggest.requested, so the first visit to New blog already has topics. Skipped when Jev is not set up.

flows.name: Suggest topics
flows.trigger: Event ideas/suggest.requested (an analysis finished, or the Suggest topics button on /drafts/new)

steps.what: Find gaps on the writer's own site: thin topics, keywords mentioned but never covered, follow-ups, pages with no links out. Leaves out any topic that already has a draft.

steps.model: cheap tier, one call for the whole batch
steps.what: Turn Scout's placeholder titles into real titles, or mark an idea as not a topic. An idea with no good title is skipped.
Score each idea 0–100 for fit with the site, and check the exclusion rules (duplicate, too close to an idea the writer rejected). Under the fit bar: skipped, with a written reason.

flows.result: A list of scored ideas. No draft is written and no draft is counted against the month.

flows.name: Write a draft by hand (Manual mode)
flows.trigger: The writer picks a suggested topic or types their own on /drafts/new → POST /api/drafts → event draft/generate.requested

steps.what: Take one draft from the month's limit (one atomic database statement) and create the draft with status generating. No slot left: nothing is written and nothing is spent.
Run the four writing agents in order. See the flow writing_pipeline.
Only if the draft failed: give the slot back, so a failure does not cost the writer a draft.

flows.name: The four writing agents
flows.trigger: Called by generate-draft, regenerate-draft and autopilot-run
flows.note: Each step saves its result. A failed draft restarts from the failed step and does not pay again for the steps before it.

steps.what: Find the writer's related posts in pgvector. With a search key set, also read up to 3 pages from other sites on the topic. Write the brief.
Write the post in the writer's voice from the style profile, the brief and real examples. One Jev score on how hard the topic is picks the tier.
Title options, meta description, slug. Internal links to the writer's own posts, ranked by Jev.
Fix grammar and clarity, keep the style consistent. Jev checks each sentence and flags claims that need a source.

flows.result: Draft with status in review. The agents cannot set any status past this.

flows.name: Review a draft
flows.trigger: The writer opens a draft on /drafts/[id]

choices.what: Change the text in the editor
Status becomes rejected. The reason is saved. Scout never proposes that topic again, and a topic-related reason is shown to the Judge.
Status becomes approved. The draft is handed to the site's publishing connection.

flows.logged: Every approve, reject, regenerate and edit is saved as feedback.

flows.name: Deliver an approved draft
flows.trigger: A draft becomes approved (the writer's click, or the run itself in Autopilot mode)
flows.rule: Only approved drafts leave the app. One draft is published once.

routes.how: The writer installs our plugin and pastes one key. The plugin calls the app: GET /api/plugin/posts → creates the post in WordPress → POST /api/plugin/posts/[draftId]/confirm. It checks every 5 minutes, and at once when nudged.
routes.lands_as: A WordPress draft, or a live post if the site owner chose Publish in the plugin's settings

routes.how: WordPress username + Application Password. The app pushes the post through the WordPress REST API.
Copy or download the approved draft as HTML or Markdown

flows.result: Draft with status published once the site confirms the post

flows.name: Autopilot: the same work on a schedule
flows.trigger: Cron 0 2 * * * (02:00 UTC, 07:30 in India), or the Run now button → event autopilot/run.requested

modes.needs: A connection that puts posts live: the WordPress plugin set to Publish

steps.what: Close free months that have ended
Check paid plans that may have ended
Pick the sites with Autopilot on, not paused, and due by their cadence. Send one autopilot/run.requested for each.
Refuse to start if the writing models or Jev are not set up. Make sure this month's usage record exists.
Claim the site (one run at a time), re-read the settings, then Scout → Naming → Judge (as in suggest_topics), then the writing_pipeline for each idea that passed, up to the weekly and monthly limits
Autopilot mode only: approve the drafts this run wrote and hand them to the site, through the same code as the Approve button. In Semi-autopilot the drafts wait in review.

flows.name: Plans and payment
flows.trigger: The writer chooses a plan on /pricing

steps.what: Checkout
Payment is confirmed and the plan and its monthly draft limit are updated

rules: Nothing reaches a site without an approval. In Manual and Semi-autopilot the writer approves. In Autopilot mode the run approves its own drafts, and only for a site whose owner chose that.
The writing agents cannot publish. They stop at in review.
Every skipped idea keeps a written reason, shown on the dashboard.
An idea the Judge could not score is skipped, never written.
Limits are checked before any model is called. A run at its limit costs nothing.
One Autopilot run per site at a time. A second run waits.
A run stops after 2 drafts in a row fail.
A topic that already has a draft is not proposed again. A rejection is remembered.
Once a person has seen a draft, a retry cannot overwrite it.
Every model call is recorded with provider, model, tokens and cost.
